topic: Which battery makes better use of its input?
prior: Can read energy in kilowatt-hours, but may not know what efficiency divides by.
objective: Compare energy returned with energy put in for each complete cycle and explain why the ranking can change.
takeaway: Compare the fraction returned, rather than the number of kilowatt-hours alone.
tone: Curious and conversational; pronounce the quantities clearly.

intro.description: Pose a fair comparison with the input readings unknown.
intro.must_show: Two batteries with their returned energy; input readings hidden.

lesson.description: Reveal why the input values matter.
lesson.must_show: The same batteries with both input meters revealed.

mechanism.description: Calculate each return as a share of its own input.
mechanism.must_show: Both division expressions and their percentages.

result.description: Answer which returns the larger share and distinguish the amount.
result.must_show: Keep both worked ratios visible while stating the conclusion.

transfer.question: A third battery takes in fifty and returns forty kilowatt-hours. What share is that?
transfer.reasoning: Forty divided by fifty is four fifths.

facts.claim: Battery B takes in 120 kWh and returns 84 kWh. Battery A takes in 60 kWh and returns 48 kWh. Both are complete cycles measured at the same electrical boundary.

constraints: Do not infer power, capacity, product quality or cause of losses.
